subject: Reserved GPU readiness signals — summary and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Cho <amanda@vehiclepay.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved GPU readiness signals — summary and next steps

Hi Amanda — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking through VehiclePay's latency pain and the projected growth numbers. I promised a short recap + proposed next steps so your procurement and infra teams have a single reference.

Key pain points you confirmed
- Highly variable tail latency during peak reconciliation windows (spikes to ~700ms at 99th).
- Inconsistent throughput under burst loads from batch reprocessing (from 50 TPS baseline -> short bursts to 800 TPS).
- Data isolation requirements for payment tokens: VPC + allocated GPU pools preferred (audit requirement).

Current stack / constraints you shared
- Inference: private model hosted on GCP VMs using a mix of CPU and single-GPU endpoints.
- KV cache approach: local warmup with poor cold-start behavior when workers scale up.
- Compliance: SOC2-in-progress; procurement needs explicit audit log and KMS integration notes.

Success criteria for a Dedicated reservation (what would make this a go)
- Predictable 99th percentile latency <= 200ms at steady-state load.
- Capacity headroom to absorb 3× peak bursts for up to 90s without request loss (autoscale or burst policy).
- Dedicated GPU pools with tenant isolation and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS.
- Clear SLOs and a runbook for graceful fallback to hosted API during maintenance.

Signals of readiness (what we can validate in a technical POC)
- End-to-end 30-minute load run showing 99p latency across sustained 200 TPS with intermittent 600–800 TPS spikes.
- KV cache warmup improvement: cold-start 99p reduces by at least 40% using pinned warm workers / prefix caching.
- Observable audit events delivered to your SIEM (sample logs during POC).

Recommended next steps
1) Tech POC scope (2 weeks): reserved pool for 2–3 GPUs, run the spike test, and validate KV/cache warmup improvements. I attached a one-page checklist for the POC.
2) Procurement packet: I'll send the template with SLA language and KMS integration details — pick a contact from procurement and I'll loop them in (cc: procurement@vehiclepay.com).
3) Follow-up call: 11/25 Tuesday, 10am PT to review POC plan and agree on success metrics.

Attachments: vehiclepay-sla-questions.pdf (procurement checklist), rsvp-dedicated-readiness-checklist.xlsx (POC tests & metrics).

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll reach out to schedule the POC kickoff and share the procurement template.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

Thanks Naomi — helpful recap. Couple of clarifications from our side:
- We absolutely need isolation for payment token handling; "shared tenancy" within a VPC is okay only if clear GPU-level allocation is guaranteed.
- The "3x peak" headroom is aggressive. Can we start with 2x headroom for the POC and then tune? Procurement wants to see cost delta for 2x vs 3x.
- Our compliance lead (cc'd) wants to confirm that audit logs include per-request model version and kv-cache hits/misses.

For the POC: we can allocate a test dataset and a staging network slice; procurement will confirm budgetary approvals this week. 11/25 10am PT works for our infra lead — please send a calendar invite.

Amanda
